source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.

records.literal_gloss: It came about now in Iconium together [for] them to enter into the synagogue of the Jews and to speak so that to believe of Jews both and of Greeks a great multitude.

en.L: Now it happened in Iconium that they went together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.
en.B: In Iconium the two of them went together into the synagogue of the Jews. They spoke in such a way that a large crowd of Jews and Greeks believed.
en.R: In the city of Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue. They spoke so well that a great many Jews and Greeks believed in Jesus.

fr.L: Or il arriva à Iconium qu’ils entrèrent ensemble dans la synagogue des Juifs et parlèrent de telle manière qu’une grande multitude de Juifs et de Grecs crut.
fr.B: À Iconium, les deux hommes entrèrent ensemble dans la synagogue des Juifs. Ils parlèrent de telle façon qu’un grand nombre de Juifs et de Grecs crurent.
fr.R: Dans la ville d’Iconium, Paul et Barnabas sont entrés ensemble dans la synagogue juive. Ils ont si bien parlé que beaucoup de Juifs et de Grecs ont cru en Jésus.

es.L: Y sucedió en Iconio que entraron juntos en la sinagoga de los judíos y hablaron de tal manera que creyó una gran multitud de judíos y de griegos.
es.B: En Iconio, los dos entraron juntos en la sinagoga de los judíos. Hablaron de tal manera que creyó una gran multitud de judíos y de griegos.
es.R: En la ciudad de Iconio, Pablo y Bernabé fueron juntos a la sinagoga de los judíos. Hablaron tan bien que muchísimos judíos y griegos creyeron en Jesús.

sw.L: Basi ikawa huko Ikonio waliingia pamoja katika sinagogi la Wayahudi, wakanena kwa namna ambayo umati mkubwa wa Wayahudi na wa Wagiriki uliamini.
sw.B: Huko Ikonio wale wawili waliingia pamoja katika sinagogi la Wayahudi. Walihubiri kwa namna ambayo kundi kubwa la Wayahudi na Wagiriki liliamini.
sw.R: Katika mji wa Ikonio, Paulo na Barnaba waliingia pamoja katika sinagogi la Wayahudi. Walizungumza vizuri sana hata Wayahudi wengi na Wagiriki wengi wakamwamini Yesu.

decisions.choice: Iconium: a city east of Pisidian Antioch, on the main Roman road across the region
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas came here after being driven out of Pisidian Antioch (13:50-51). The city is the modern Konya in Turkey.

decisions.choice: together: the two went in together
alternatives: in the same way, as at Antioch
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "together" or "in the same way". "In the same way" would point back to their custom at Antioch (13:14). Both readings fit, and the difference is small.

decisions.choice: Greeks: non-Jews, probably those who attended the synagogue
decisions.reason: They are set beside Jews, so they are Gentiles. Since they were in the synagogue, they were probably Gentiles who worshiped Israel's God, like those in 13:16 and 13:26.

decisions.choice: believed in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they believed in, as the message of 13:38-39 makes clear.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), with Luke's historic presents kept at Literal
decisions.reason: As in Acts 1: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé throughout, as French is spoken and read in school today. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level (the passé composé in Paul's speech at Lystra, 14:15-17). This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: Wagiriki
decisions.reason: The Greek names Greeks, here non-Jews who probably came to the synagogue (meaning decision); "Wagiriki" keeps the name, as in 17:4, and "watu wa mataifa" stays for the Greek word for Gentiles in 14:2.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The but having disobeyed Jews stirred up and made evil the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.

en.L: But the Jews who disobeyed stirred up and embittered the minds of the Gentiles against the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned their minds against the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles. They made them angry with the believers.

fr.L: Mais les Juifs qui avaient désobéi excitèrent et aigrirent les esprits des nations contre les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.B: Mais les Juifs qui refusaient de croire excitèrent les non-Juifs et les montèrent contre les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: Mais les Juifs qui refusaient de croire ont excité les non-Juifs. Ils les ont mis en colère contre les croyants.

es.L: Pero los judíos que desobedecieron incitaron y envenenaron los ánimos de los gentiles contra los hermanos.
es.B: Pero los judíos que se negaron a creer incitaron a los gentiles y les envenenaron el ánimo contra los hermanos.
es.R: Pero los judíos que no quisieron creer alborotaron a los gentiles. Hicieron que se enojaran con los creyentes.

sw.L: Lakini Wayahudi waliokataa kutii waliichochea na kuitia uchungu mioyo ya watu wa mataifa dhidi ya ndugu.
sw.B: Lakini Wayahudi waliokataa kuamini waliwachochea watu wa mataifa, wakaitia sumu mioyo yao dhidi ya ndugu.
sw.R: Lakini Wayahudi waliokataa kuamini waliwachochea watu wa mataifa. Wakawafanya wawakasirikie waumini.

decisions.choice: who disobeyed: who refused to believe the message
decisions.reason: In the New Testament refusing to obey the message and refusing to believe it go together (John 3:36; Hebrews 3:18-19). Here it is set against the many who believed (14:1).

decisions.choice: made their souls evil: poisoned their minds, made them hostile
decisions.reason: The verb means to do harm or to make bad. With "souls" it means turning their thinking and feelings against someone.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the believers in Iconium, men and women, together with Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: Acts calls fellow believers brothers (1:15; 9:30). The new believers of 14:1 are the ones the hostility is aimed at, along with their teachers.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the shorter text
alternatives: Codex Bezae and related witnesses expand the verse
decisions.reason: The Western text, chiefly Codex Bezae, says the leaders of the synagogue and the rulers stirred up persecution against the righteous, and adds that the Lord soon gave peace. The SBLGNT follows the shorter text found in most manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the New Testament: Literal keeps the Greek word "nations"; Balanced and Readable say plainly who is meant. "Les païens" now sounds pejorative and "les Gentils" is church jargon.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 3:17: Spanish "hermanos" already takes in the women among the believers (meaning decision on the brothers).

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender span
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already includes sisters, so Swahili has no second wording for the English gender setting; the same wherever the English has a gender span in this chapter ("wanadamu" in 14:11 and 14:15, "Enyi watu" in 14:15).

source.text: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: A long indeed therefore time they stayed speaking boldly upon the Lord, the [one] bearing witness to the word of the grace of him, giving signs and wonders to happen through the hands of them.

en.L: So they stayed a considerable time, speaking boldly [in reliance] on the Lord, who bore witness to the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, granting signs and wonders to be done through their hands.
en.B: So they stayed there a long time and spoke boldly, relying on the Lord. He bore witness to the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace by allowing signs and wonders to happen through their hands.
en.R: Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time. They were not afraid to speak, because they trusted the Lord. The Lord showed that their message about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace was true. He did this by letting them do signs and wonders.

fr.L: Ils séjournèrent donc assez longtemps, parlant avec assurance, [appuyés] sur le Seigneur, qui rendait témoignage à la parole de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, accordant que des signes et des prodiges se produisent par leurs mains.
fr.B: Ils restèrent donc là longtemps et parlèrent avec assurance, confiants dans le Seigneur. Il rendait témoignage à la parole de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce en permettant que des signes et des prodiges se produisent par leurs mains.
fr.R: Paul et Barnabas sont restés là longtemps. Ils parlaient sans peur, parce qu’ils avaient confiance dans le Seigneur. Le Seigneur montrait que leur message sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce était vrai. Pour cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur permettait de faire des signes et des prodiges.

es.L: Así que se quedaron bastante tiempo, hablando con valentía, [confiados] en el Señor, que daba testimonio a la palabra de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, concediendo que se hicieran señales y prodigios por medio de sus manos.
es.B: Así que se quedaron allí mucho tiempo y hablaban con valentía, confiados en el Señor. Él confirmaba el mensaje de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, haciendo que por manos de ellos se realizaran señales y prodigios.
es.R: Pablo y Bernabé se quedaron allí mucho tiempo. No tenían miedo de hablar, porque confiaban en el Señor. El Señor mostraba que el mensaje que anunciaban acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia era verdad. Lo hacía permitiéndoles hacer señales y maravillas.

sw.L: Basi walikaa [huko] muda mrefu, wakinena kwa ujasiri [wakimtegemea] Bwana, aliyelishuhudia neno la neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akiwajalia ishara na maajabu kutendeka kwa mikono yao.
sw.B: Basi walikaa huko muda mrefu, wakinena kwa ujasiri, wakimtegemea Bwana. Bwana alilishuhudia neno la neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa kuwajalia ishara na maajabu kutendeka kwa mikono yao.
sw.R: Paulo na Barnaba walikaa huko muda mrefu. Hawakuogopa kuhubiri, kwa sababu walimtegemea Bwana. Bwana alionyesha kwamba ujumbe wao kuhusu neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ni wa kweli. Alifanya hivyo kwa kuwawezesha kufanya ishara na maajabu.

decisions.choice: so: the success of 14:1 is why they stayed, in spite of the opposition of 14:2
decisions.reason: The words pick up the story again after the aside in 14:2. The many who believed gave them reason to stay, and the hostility did not drive them out at once.

decisions.choice: speaking boldly on the Lord: speaking openly, relying on the Lord
decisions.reason: The preposition with this verb means trusting in or resting on someone. Their boldness came from confidence in the Lord.

decisions.choice: the Lord: probably the risen Jesus, who confirms the message about his grace
decisions.reason: In Acts "the Lord" is often Jesus (1:21; 11:20-21). In 20:32 "the word of his grace" is God's. The text does not say which is meant, and the sense is the same: the message comes from the Lord and he backs it.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the Lord's own testimony that the message is true
alternatives: proof of the apostles' own power
decisions.reason: The Lord is the one who grants the signs; the apostles' hands are only the means. Hebrews 2:4 says God bore witness in the same way. Peter denies that such power is their own (3:12).

decisions.choice: The Lord showed that their message about his grace was true
alternatives: bore witness to the word of his grace
decisions.reason: Readable explains what bearing witness to the word means.

decisions.choice: des signes et des prodiges
decisions.reason: "Signe" stays the word for a sign, never "miracle", as in John; "prodige" is the usual French word for an astonishing wonder and keeps the pair distinct.

source.text: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.

records.literal_gloss: Was divided but the multitude of the city, and some were with the Jews, some but with the apostles.

en.L: But the multitude of the city was divided, and some were with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
en.B: The people of the city were split: some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
en.R: The people in the city could not agree. Some were on the side of the Jews who opposed Paul and Barnabas. Others were on the side of the apostles.

fr.L: Mais la multitude de la ville se divisa : les uns étaient avec les Juifs, les autres avec les apôtres.
fr.B: La population de la ville se partagea : les uns prirent le parti des Juifs, les autres celui des apôtres.
fr.R: Les gens de la ville n’étaient pas d’accord entre eux. Certains étaient du côté des Juifs qui s’opposaient à Paul et à Barnabas. D’autres étaient du côté des apôtres.

es.L: Pero la multitud de la ciudad se dividió, y unos estaban con los judíos, y otros con los apóstoles.
es.B: La gente de la ciudad se dividió: unos se pusieron del lado de los judíos, y otros del lado de los apóstoles.
es.R: La gente de la ciudad no se ponía de acuerdo. Algunos estaban del lado de los judíos que se oponían a Pablo y a Bernabé. Otros estaban del lado de los apóstoles.

sw.L: Lakini umati wa mji uligawanyika, na wengine walikuwa pamoja na Wayahudi, na wengine pamoja na mitume.
sw.B: Watu wa mji waligawanyika: wengine waliwaunga mkono Wayahudi, na wengine mitume.
sw.R: Watu wa mji hawakukubaliana. Wengine waliwaunga mkono Wayahudi waliowapinga Paulo na Barnaba. Wengine waliwaunga mkono mitume.

decisions.choice: were with: took the side of
decisions.reason: The city split into two parties.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jews who refused to believe (14:2)
decisions.reason: Many Jews in Iconium had believed (14:1). Luke means the opponents.

decisions.choice: the apostles: Paul and Barnabas, sent out by the church (see 14:14)
decisions.reason: This is the first time Acts calls Paul and Barnabas apostles. The decision on 14:14 explains the sense.

decisions.choice: the Jews who opposed Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear which Jews are meant, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς, συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον, κἀκεῖ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν.

records.literal_gloss: When but there was a rush of the Gentiles both and Jews with the rulers of them to mistreat and to stone them, \v 6 having become aware they fled to the cities of the Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region, \v 7 and there preaching the gospel they were.

en.L: And when a move was made by both the Gentiles and Jews with their rulers to mistreat and to stone them, \v 6 they became aware [of it] and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region, \v 7 and there they were preaching the gospel.
en.B: When Gentiles and Jews, with their rulers, set out to abuse the apostles and stone them, \v 6 the apostles learned of it and escaped to Lystra and Derbe, towns of Lycaonia, and to the country around them. \v 7 There they kept on proclaiming the gospel.
en.R: Then some Gentiles and Jews, and their leaders too, made a plan. They wanted to hurt Paul and Barnabas and kill them by throwing stones at them. \v 6 But Paul and Barnabas found out about it. They ran away to Lystra and Derbe, towns in the area called Lycaonia, and to the land around them. \v 7 There they kept telling people the good news.

fr.L: Et comme il y eut un mouvement des nations et des Juifs, avec leurs chefs, pour les maltraiter et [les] lapider, \v 6 s’en étant rendu compte, ils se réfugièrent dans les villes de Lycaonie, Lystre et Derbe, et dans la région environnante, \v 7 et là ils annonçaient l’Évangile.
fr.B: Comme des non-Juifs et des Juifs, avec leurs chefs, s’apprêtaient à maltraiter les apôtres et à les lapider, \v 6 ceux-ci l’apprirent et s’enfuirent à Lystre et à Derbe, villes de Lycaonie, et dans la région alentour. \v 7 Là, ils continuèrent d’annoncer l’Évangile.
fr.R: Alors des non-Juifs et des Juifs, avec leurs chefs, ont formé un projet. Ils voulaient faire du mal à Paul et à Barnabas, et les tuer en leur jetant des pierres. \v 6 Mais Paul et Barnabas l’ont appris. Ils se sont enfuis à Lystre et à Derbe, des villes de la région appelée Lycaonie, et dans les environs. \v 7 Là, ils ont continué à annoncer la bonne nouvelle.

es.L: Y cuando hubo un intento tanto de los gentiles como de los judíos, con sus gobernantes, de maltratarlos y apedrearlos, \v 6 dándose cuenta [de ello], huyeron a las ciudades de Licaonia, Listra y Derbe, y a la región circunvecina, \v 7 y allí anunciaban la buena noticia.
es.B: Cuando gentiles y judíos, junto con sus gobernantes, se lanzaron a maltratar a los apóstoles y apedrearlos, \v 6 ellos se enteraron y huyeron a Listra y Derbe, ciudades de Licaonia, y a la región de los alrededores. \v 7 Allí siguieron anunciando la buena noticia.
es.R: Entonces algunos gentiles y judíos, junto con sus líderes, hicieron un plan. Querían maltratar a Pablo y a Bernabé y matarlos a pedradas. \v 6 Pero Pablo y Bernabé se enteraron. Huyeron a Listra y Derbe, ciudades de la región llamada Licaonia, y a los alrededores. \v 7 Allí siguieron contándole a la gente la buena noticia.

sw.L: Na ulipotokea mpango wa watu wa mataifa na wa Wayahudi pamoja na wakuu wao wa kuwatendea jeuri na kuwapiga kwa mawe, \v 6 wao wakiisha kuutambua, walikimbilia miji ya Likaonia, Listra na Derbe, na eneo lililozunguka, \v 7 na huko walikuwa wakihubiri habari njema.
sw.B: Watu wa mataifa na Wayahudi, pamoja na viongozi wao, walipokuwa wakijiandaa kuwatendea mitume jeuri na kuwapiga kwa mawe, \v 6 mitume walipata habari, wakakimbilia Listra na Derbe, miji ya Likaonia, na eneo lililoizunguka. \v 7 Huko waliendelea kuhubiri habari njema.
sw.R: Kisha baadhi ya watu wa mataifa na Wayahudi, pamoja na viongozi wao, walifanya mpango. Walitaka kuwaumiza Paulo na Barnaba na kuwaua kwa kuwapiga mawe. \v 6 Lakini Paulo na Barnaba walipata habari hiyo. Wakakimbilia Listra na Derbe, miji iliyo katika eneo liitwalo Likaonia, na katika nchi iliyoizunguka. \v 7 Huko waliendelea kuwaambia watu habari njema.

decisions.choice: a move: an attempt that was under way, not yet carried out
decisions.reason: The word means a rush or an impulse to act. The apostles learned of it and left before it was carried out (14:6).

decisions.choice: their rulers: the leaders on both sides, city officials and synagogue leaders
decisions.reason: The pronoun may refer to the Jews or to both groups. Either way, people in authority took part.

decisions.choice: to stone: to kill by throwing stones
alternatives: to throw a few stones as an insult
decisions.reason: Stoning was the penalty the law set for blasphemy (Leviticus 24:16), as with Stephen (7:58). Here it would have been mob violence.

decisions.choice: Lycaonia: a region to the east; Lystra and Derbe were its towns
decisions.reason: Xenophon (Anabasis 1.2.19) calls Iconium the last city of Phrygia, so in fleeing to Lystra they crossed into another region. Lystra was a Roman colony, founded under Augustus.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the verse ends with their preaching
alternatives: Codex Bezae adds that the whole crowd was moved by the teaching and that Paul and Barnabas stayed in Lystra
decisions.reason: The addition is found in the Western text. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: kill them by throwing stones at them
decisions.reason: Readable says what stoning meant.

decisions.choice: annoncer l’Évangile (L, B); annoncer la bonne nouvelle (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles: "l’Évangile" at Literal and Balanced, "la bonne nouvelle" at Readable, as the English Readable says "good news". "Évangéliser" is church jargon and "prêcher" loses the link with the good news.

decisions.choice: anunciaban la buena noticia
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, 13:32 and 16:10: the verb "to tell good news" is "anunciar la buena noticia" in Acts; the noun "evangelio" is kept for the noun.

decisions.choice: Likaonia, Listra, Derbe
decisions.reason: The region and its towns in the usual Swahili spelling of these names, as "Listra" and "Derbe" in 16:1; the same through the chapter (and "Kilikaonia" for the language in 14:11).

source.text: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν.

records.literal_gloss: And a certain man without strength in Lystra in the feet was sitting, lame from [the] womb of [the] mother of him, who never had walked.

en.L: And in Lystra a certain man was sitting [who was] without strength in [his] feet, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
en.B: At Lystra there was a man sitting who could not use his feet. He had been lame since birth and had never taken a step.
en.R: In Lystra there was a man who could not walk. He had been born that way, and he had never walked at all.

fr.L: Et un homme, à Lystre, était assis, impotent des pieds, boiteux dès le sein de sa mère, qui n’avait jamais marché.
fr.B: À Lystre se tenait assis un homme qui ne pouvait pas se servir de ses pieds. Il était infirme de naissance et n’avait jamais fait un pas.
fr.R: À Lystre, il y avait un homme qui ne pouvait pas marcher. Il était né ainsi, et il n’avait jamais marché de sa vie.

es.L: Y en Listra estaba sentado cierto hombre sin fuerza en los pies, cojo desde el vientre de su madre, que nunca había caminado.
es.B: En Listra había un hombre sentado que no podía usar los pies. Era cojo de nacimiento y nunca había dado un paso.
es.R: En Listra había un hombre que no podía caminar. Había nacido así y nunca había caminado.

sw.L: Na huko Listra mtu mmoja alikuwa ameketi, [aliyekuwa] hana nguvu miguuni, kiwete tangu tumboni mwa mama yake, ambaye hakuwa ametembea kamwe.
sw.B: Huko Listra kulikuwa na mtu mmoja aliyekuwa ameketi, asiyeweza kutumia miguu yake. Alikuwa kiwete tangu kuzaliwa, wala hakuwa amewahi kupiga hatua hata moja.
sw.R: Katika mji wa Listra kulikuwa na mtu mmoja ambaye hakuweza kutembea. Alizaliwa akiwa hivyo, na hakuwa amewahi kutembea hata siku moja.

decisions.choice: from his mother's womb: from birth
alternatives: since he was a small child
decisions.reason: A common Hebrew way of saying from birth (Psalm 22:11; Judges 16:17). The same words describe the lame man in 3:2.

decisions.choice: a healing like Peter's in 3:1-10
decisions.reason: Both men were lame from birth; both apostles fix their eyes on the man; both men leap up and walk (3:4, 3:8; 14:9-10). Luke shows Paul doing the same works as Peter.

decisions.choice: three descriptions that stress how hopeless his case was
decisions.reason: Without strength in his feet, lame from birth, never had walked: the repetition makes the healing all the more striking.

source.text: οὗτος ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ· Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός· καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.

records.literal_gloss: This one heard the Paul speaking, who having looked intently at him and having seen that he has faith to be saved, \v 10 said with a loud voice, Stand up on the feet of you upright. And he sprang up and was walking.

en.L: This [man] was listening to Paul speaking. [Paul], fixing his eyes on him and seeing that he had faith to be made well, \v 10 said with a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet." And he leaped up and began walking.
en.B: The man was listening while Paul spoke. Paul fixed his eyes on him and saw that he had faith that he would be made well. \v 10 So he said in a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet!" And the man leaped up and walked.
en.R: This man listened to Paul as he spoke. Paul looked hard at him and saw that the man had faith that God could heal him. \v 10 So Paul shouted, "Stand up straight on your feet!" The man jumped up and began to walk.

fr.L: Celui-ci écoutait Paul parler. [Paul], fixant les yeux sur lui et voyant qu’il avait la foi pour être guéri, \v 10 dit d’une voix forte : « Lève-toi droit sur tes pieds. » Et il bondit et se mit à marcher.
fr.B: L’homme écoutait Paul pendant qu’il parlait. Paul fixa les yeux sur lui et vit qu’il avait la foi pour être guéri. \v 10 Il lui dit alors d’une voix forte : « Lève-toi, tiens-toi droit sur tes pieds ! » Et l’homme bondit et se mit à marcher.
fr.R: Cet homme écoutait Paul pendant qu’il parlait. Paul l’a regardé attentivement et a vu que l’homme croyait que Dieu pouvait le guérir. \v 10 Alors Paul a crié : « Lève-toi et tiens-toi bien droit sur tes pieds ! » L’homme a sauté sur ses pieds et s’est mis à marcher.

es.L: Este escuchaba hablar a Pablo; el cual, fijando en él la mirada y viendo que tenía fe para ser sanado, \v 10 dijo con gran voz: «Ponte derecho sobre tus pies». Y él dio un salto y comenzó a caminar.
es.B: El hombre escuchaba mientras Pablo hablaba. Pablo lo miró fijamente y vio que tenía fe para ser sanado. \v 10 Entonces le dijo en voz alta: «¡Ponte de pie, derecho!». Y el hombre dio un salto y echó a andar.
es.R: Este hombre escuchaba a Pablo mientras hablaba. Pablo lo miró fijamente y vio que el hombre tenía fe en que Dios podía sanarlo. \v 10 Entonces Pablo le gritó: «¡Levántate y ponte derecho sobre tus pies!». El hombre dio un salto y comenzó a caminar.

sw.L: Huyu alikuwa akimsikiliza Paulo akinena. [Paulo], akimkazia macho na kuona kwamba ana imani ya kuponywa, \v 10 alisema kwa sauti kuu, "Simama wima kwa miguu yako." Naye akaruka juu, akaanza kutembea.
sw.B: Mtu huyo alikuwa akimsikiliza Paulo alipokuwa akihubiri. Paulo alimkazia macho, akaona kwamba alikuwa na imani ya kuponywa. \v 10 Basi akasema kwa sauti kuu, "Simama wima kwa miguu yako!" Yule mtu akaruka juu, akaanza kutembea.
sw.R: Mtu huyo alimsikiliza Paulo alipokuwa akizungumza. Paulo alimtazama sana, akaona kwamba mtu huyo aliamini kwamba Mungu angeweza kumponya. \v 10 Kwa hiyo Paulo alipaza sauti, "Simama wima kwa miguu yako!" Yule mtu akaruka juu, akaanza kutembea.

decisions.choice: fixing his eyes: looking at him steadily
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same verb of Peter looking at the lame man (3:4) and of Paul facing Elymas (13:9).

decisions.choice: to be made well: to be healed, with a hint of the wider sense, to be saved
alternatives: to be saved from sin only
decisions.reason: The verb is used of healing (4:9; Luke 8:48) and of salvation (4:12). Here the healing is meant, but in Acts it points to the salvation Paul was preaching.

decisions.choice: he leaped up and walked: like the lame man in 3:8, and Isaiah 35:6
decisions.reason: Isaiah 35:6 promises that in God's day the lame will leap like a deer. Acts 3:8 uses the same picture.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: Paul's command alone
alternatives: Codex Bezae adds "I say to you in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: The Western text adds the name, perhaps from 3:6. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: faith that God could heal him
decisions.reason: Readable says who would heal him; Paul's message (14:15) points to God.

decisions.choice: être guéri
decisions.reason: The verb can mean both to be healed and to be saved (m2). The sentence is about his feet, so French says "guéri", as the English says "made well"; "sauvé" would make the healing sound secondary.

decisions.choice: kuponywa
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made well, with a hint of being saved (meaning decision). Here the man's need is his feet, so "kuponywa" (to be healed) says what he hoped for; "kuokolewa" would lose the healing.

source.text: οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες· Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρναβᾶν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.

records.literal_gloss: The and crowds having seen what did Paul lifted up the voice of them in Lycaonian saying, The gods having been made like to men have come down to us, \v 12 they were calling and the Barnabas Zeus, the and Paul Hermes, since he was the [one] leading of the word.

en.L: And the crowds, seeing what Paul had done, lifted up their voice in Lycaonian, saying, "The gods have become like {{gender:humans|men}} and have come down to us!" \v 12 And they called Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, since he was the one leading in the speaking.
en.B: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices in the Lycaonian language: "The gods have become like humans and come down to us!" \v 12 They began calling Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, because Paul was the one who took the lead in speaking.
en.R: The crowds saw what Paul had done. They began to shout in their own language, Lycaonian. They said, "The gods have made themselves look like humans, and they have come down to us!" \v 12 They called Barnabas by the name of the god Zeus. They called Paul Hermes, the god who carried messages for the gods, because Paul did most of the talking.

fr.L: Et les foules, voyant ce que Paul avait fait, élevèrent leur voix en lycaonien, disant : « Les dieux, s’étant rendus semblables aux {{gender:humains|hommes}}, sont descendus vers nous ! » \v 12 Et ils appelaient Barnabas Zeus, et Paul Hermès, puisque c’était lui qui portait la parole.
fr.B: Quand les foules virent ce que Paul avait fait, elles s’écrièrent en langue lycaonienne : « Les dieux ont pris forme humaine et sont descendus jusqu’à nous ! » \v 12 Elles se mirent à appeler Barnabas Zeus, et Paul Hermès, parce que c’était Paul qui portait la parole.
fr.R: Les gens ont vu ce que Paul avait fait. Ils se sont mis à crier dans leur langue, le lycaonien. Ils disaient : « Les dieux ont pris l’apparence d’êtres humains, et ils sont descendus chez nous ! » \v 12 Ils ont appelé Barnabas du nom du dieu Zeus. Ils ont appelé Paul Hermès, le dieu qui portait les messages des dieux, parce que c’était Paul qui parlait le plus.

es.L: Y las multitudes, viendo lo que Pablo había hecho, alzaron su voz, diciendo en licaonio: «¡Los dioses, hechos semejantes a {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, han descendido a nosotros!». \v 12 Y llamaban a Bernabé Zeus, y a Pablo Hermes, porque él era el que dirigía la palabra.
es.B: Cuando la gente vio lo que Pablo había hecho, gritó en el idioma de Licaonia: «¡Los dioses se han hecho como seres humanos y han bajado hasta nosotros!». \v 12 A Bernabé lo llamaban Zeus, y a Pablo, Hermes, porque era él quien llevaba la palabra.
es.R: La gente vio lo que Pablo había hecho. Comenzaron a gritar en su propio idioma, el licaonio. Decían: «¡Los dioses se han hecho parecidos a los seres humanos y han bajado hasta nosotros!». \v 12 A Bernabé le pusieron el nombre del dios Zeus. A Pablo lo llamaron Hermes, el dios que llevaba los mensajes de los dioses, porque Pablo era el que más hablaba.

sw.L: Na makutano, walipoona alichokifanya Paulo, walipaza sauti zao kwa Kilikaonia, wakisema, "Miungu, wakiwa wamefanana na wanadamu, wameshuka kwetu!" \v 12 Wakawa wakimwita Barnaba Zeusi, na Paulo Herme, kwa kuwa yeye ndiye aliyekuwa akiongoza katika kunena.
sw.B: Makutano walipoona alichofanya Paulo, walipaza sauti zao kwa lugha ya Kilikaonia, "Miungu wamechukua umbo la wanadamu, wameshuka kwetu!" \v 12 Wakaanza kumwita Barnaba Zeusi, na Paulo Herme, kwa sababu Paulo ndiye aliyekuwa msemaji mkuu.
sw.R: Watu wengi walioona alichofanya Paulo walianza kupiga kelele kwa lugha yao wenyewe, Kilikaonia. Wakasema, "Miungu wamejifanya kuwa kama wanadamu, nao wameshuka kwetu!" \v 12 Wakamwita Barnaba kwa jina la mungu Zeusi. Wakamwita Paulo Herme, mungu aliyepeleka ujumbe wa miungu, kwa sababu Paulo ndiye aliyezungumza zaidi.

decisions.choice: in Lycaonian: in the local language, not in Greek
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas spoke Greek. The crowd's own language may explain why the apostles did not at first understand what was happening, and acted only when they heard of the sacrifice (14:14).

decisions.choice: the gods have become like humans: they have taken human form
alternatives: the gods have sent men like themselves
decisions.reason: The crowd believes the gods themselves are present in human form.

decisions.choice: Zeus and Hermes: the chief Greek god and his messenger
alternatives: Jupiter and Mercury, their Latin names
decisions.reason: Zeus was the father and ruler of the gods; Hermes was their messenger and spokesman. The Roman poet Ovid (Metamorphoses 8.611-724) tells a story set in the neighboring region of Phrygia in which Jupiter and Mercury (Zeus and Hermes) visited in human form, and only an old couple welcomed them. The crowd may have meant not to miss the gods a second time.

decisions.choice: the one leading in the speaking: the chief speaker
decisions.reason: Paul did the talking, which fitted Hermes, the god of speech. Barnabas, perhaps the older or more dignified, was taken for Zeus.

decisions.choice: Zeus and Hermes
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Greek names, and readers know them. Older English Bibles such as the King James Version use the Latin names Jupiter and Mercury.

decisions.choice: humans, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as opposed to gods. Balanced and Readable say "humans" with no setting.

decisions.choice: the god who carried messages for the gods
decisions.reason: Readable explains who Hermes was, so that the reason given makes sense.

decisions.choice: c’était lui qui portait la parole
alternatives: c’était lui qui conduisait la parole
il était le chef de la parole
decisions.reason: "Porter la parole" is the French idiom for speaking on behalf of a group, which is what the Greek phrase means (m4).

decisions.choice: Zeus, Hermes
decisions.reason: The Greek names of the chief god and his messenger (meaning decision); the Latin names found in older Spanish Bibles are not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}
decisions.reason: Human beings, set against gods; the inclusive form is the default and "hombres" the alternative.

decisions.choice: Zeusi, Herme
alternatives: Mshtarii, Utaridi (the planet names used in older Swahili versions)
decisions.reason: The Greek gods are named by their Greek names, so readers can find them in other books: "Zeusi" takes the final -i Swahili gives such names, and "Herme" is the same name as the believer greeted in Romans 16:14. The planet names would hide who the gods were.

decisions.choice: Miungu ... wameshuka, with personal agreement
decisions.reason: The crowd speaks of the gods as persons who came down, so the verbs take the personal agreement (wa-) rather than the class 4 (i-) of "miungu" as things.

source.text: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.

records.literal_gloss: The and priest of the Zeus being before the city, bulls and garlands to the gates having brought, with the crowds was wanting to sacrifice.

en.L: And the priest of Zeus, [whose temple] was in front of the city, having brought bulls and garlands to the gates, wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.
en.B: Zeus had a temple just in front of the city. His priest came to the gates with bulls and garlands, for he and the crowds meant to offer sacrifice.
en.R: There was a temple of Zeus just outside the city. The priest of Zeus brought bulls and wreaths of flowers to the city gates. He and the crowds wanted to kill the bulls as an offering to Paul and Barnabas.

fr.L: Et le prêtre de Zeus, [dont le temple] était devant la ville, ayant amené des taureaux et des guirlandes aux portes, voulait offrir un sacrifice avec les foules.
fr.B: Zeus avait un temple juste devant la ville. Son prêtre vint aux portes avec des taureaux et des guirlandes, car lui et les foules voulaient offrir un sacrifice.
fr.R: Il y avait un temple de Zeus juste à l’extérieur de la ville. Le prêtre de Zeus a amené des taureaux et des couronnes de fleurs aux portes de la ville. Lui et la foule voulaient tuer les taureaux pour les offrir à Paul et à Barnabas.

es.L: Y el sacerdote de Zeus, [cuyo templo] estaba delante de la ciudad, trayendo toros y guirnaldas a las puertas, quería ofrecer sacrificios junto con las multitudes.
es.B: Zeus tenía un templo justo a la entrada de la ciudad. Su sacerdote llevó toros y guirnaldas a las puertas, porque él y la multitud querían ofrecer sacrificios.
es.R: Había un templo de Zeus justo afuera de la ciudad. El sacerdote de Zeus llevó toros y coronas de flores a las puertas de la ciudad. Él y la gente querían matar los toros como ofrenda a Pablo y a Bernabé.

sw.L: Na kuhani wa Zeusi, [ambaye hekalu lake] lilikuwa mbele ya mji, akiisha kuleta mafahali na mashada ya maua malangoni, alitaka kutoa dhabihu pamoja na makutano.
sw.B: Zeusi alikuwa na hekalu mbele ya mji. Kuhani wake alileta mafahali na mashada ya maua mpaka kwenye malango ya mji, kwa kuwa yeye na makutano walikusudia kutoa dhabihu.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na hekalu la Zeusi nje kidogo ya mji. Kuhani wa Zeusi aliwaleta mafahali na mashada ya maua kwenye malango ya mji. Yeye na makutano walitaka kuwachinja mafahali hao kama sadaka kwa Paulo na Barnaba.

decisions.choice: Zeus who is before the city: Zeus as worshiped at a temple outside the city walls
alternatives: the priest stood before the city
decisions.reason: The phrase reads like a title of the local god, named after where his temple stood. Greek cities often had a temple at the entrance to the town.

decisions.choice: bulls and garlands: animals for sacrifice and wreaths to adorn them
decisions.reason: Animals brought for sacrifice were often hung with woolen or flower wreaths. The worshipers and priests might wear them too.

decisions.choice: the gates: the city gates, near the temple
alternatives: the gateway of the house where the apostles stayed
decisions.reason: The word means a gateway or porch. The temple was in front of the city, so the city gates fit best, but the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: wanted to sacrifice: they intended to, but did not
decisions.reason: The tense describes an action under way, and 14:18 shows the sacrifice was stopped.

decisions.choice: kill the bulls as an offering to Paul and Barnabas
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sacrifice was and to whom; 14:18 says "to them".

decisions.choice: mashada ya maua
decisions.reason: Wreaths to adorn the animals for sacrifice (meaning decision); "mashada ya maua" (garlands of flowers) says what they were, while "taji" would suggest crowns for people.

source.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: Having heard but the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having torn the garments of them, rushed out into the crowd crying out \v 15 and saying, Men, why these things are you doing?

en.L: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard [of it], they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out \v 15 and saying, "Men, why are you doing these things?
en.B: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it. They ripped their garments and dashed into the middle of the crowd, crying out, \v 15 "{{gender:People|Men}}, why are you doing these things?
en.R: But Barnabas and Paul, the apostles, heard about this. They tore their clothes to show how upset they were. They ran into the crowd and shouted, \v 15 "People, why are you doing this?

fr.L: Mais l’ayant appris, les apôtres Barnabas et Paul déchirèrent leurs vêtements et se précipitèrent dans la foule en criant \v 15 et en disant : « Hommes, pourquoi faites-vous ces choses ?
fr.B: Mais les apôtres Barnabas et Paul l’apprirent. Ils déchirèrent leurs vêtements et se précipitèrent au milieu de la foule en s’écriant : \v 15 « {{gender:Mes amis|Hommes}}, pourquoi faites-vous cela ?
fr.R: Mais Barnabas et Paul, les apôtres, l’ont appris. Ils ont déchiré leurs vêtements pour montrer combien ils étaient bouleversés. Ils ont couru dans la foule en criant : \v 15 « Mes amis, pourquoi faites-vous cela ?

es.L: Pero al oír[lo] los apóstoles Bernabé y Pablo, rasgaron sus ropas y se lanzaron entre la multitud, gritando \v 15 y diciendo: «Hombres, ¿por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto?
es.B: Pero los apóstoles Bernabé y Pablo se enteraron. Se rasgaron la ropa y se lanzaron en medio de la multitud, gritando: \v 15 «{{gender:Amigos|Hombres}}, ¿por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto?
es.R: Pero Bernabé y Pablo, los apóstoles, se enteraron de esto. Se rasgaron la ropa para mostrar lo afligidos que estaban. Corrieron hacia la multitud y gritaron: \v 15 «Amigos, ¿por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto?

sw.L: Lakini mitume Barnaba na Paulo waliposikia [hayo], walirarua mavazi yao, wakatoka mbio kuingia katikati ya umati, wakipiga kelele \v 15 na kusema, "Enyi watu, kwa nini mnafanya mambo haya?
sw.B: Lakini mitume Barnaba na Paulo walisikia habari hiyo. Wakararua mavazi yao, wakaingia mbio katikati ya umati wakipaza sauti, \v 15 "Enyi watu, mbona mnafanya mambo haya?
sw.R: Lakini Barnaba na Paulo, wale mitume, walisikia habari hiyo. Wakararua nguo zao kuonyesha jinsi walivyohuzunika sana. Wakakimbia katikati ya umati, wakapiga kelele, \v 15 "Enyi watu, kwa nini mnafanya hivi?

decisions.choice: apostles: men sent out on a mission, here Barnabas and Paul, sent by the church at Antioch
decisions.reason: The word means "one who is sent". Elsewhere in Acts the apostles are the Twelve (1:26; 15:2). Here and in 14:4 Luke uses the word of the two the Holy Spirit set apart and the church sent out (13:2-4). Paul himself insists that he was called an apostle by Jesus (Galatians 1:1; 1 Corinthians 9:1). Whether Luke means more than "envoys" here is not settled.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the apostles"
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae is reported to omit the word here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: tore their garments: a Jewish sign of horror at blasphemy
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes showed grief or outrage (Genesis 37:29). The high priest did it on hearing what he took for blasphemy (Mark 14:63). Being honored as gods horrified the apostles.

decisions.choice: men: a polite address to the whole crowd, men and women
decisions.reason: The crowd at the gates was the city's people (14:11, 14:13), and the speech that follows speaks to them all. The form of address is the usual one in Greek speeches; women may well have been present.

decisions.choice: People, with "Men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:12, the address goes to a mixed crowd. Literal keeps "Men".

decisions.choice: to show how upset they were
decisions.reason: Readable says what the action meant.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Mes amis|Hommes}} at Balanced; "Mes amis" plainly at Readable
decisions.reason: The address goes to a mixed crowd (m4). French has no plain "People" as a polite address; "Mes amis" is the natural inclusive one, with the traditional "Hommes" as the alternative, as the English has "People" / "Men". Literal keeps "Hommes".

decisions.choice: {{gender:Amigos|Hombres}} (B); Amigos (R)
decisions.reason: A polite address to the whole crowd, men and women (meaning decision on men); "Amigos" is the natural Spanish way to address a mixed crowd politely, with the traditional "Hombres" as the alternative at Balanced.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}
decisions.reason: Barnabas and Paul speak to the crowd until 14:17, so every plural "you" is the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: Enyi watu
decisions.reason: The Greek address "men" is a polite way to speak to the whole crowd, men and women (meaning decision). "Enyi wanaume" would address the males only, so Swahili says "Enyi watu" at every level, with no gender span.

source.text: καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Also we of like nature are to you men, preaching the gospel to you from these the vain [things] to turn to God living, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the [things] in them;

en.L: We also are {{gender:humans|men}} of like nature with you, proclaiming the gospel to you, that you should turn from these empty things to [the] living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the [things] in them;
en.B: We are mortals with the same nature as you. We have come with the gospel, calling you to turn away from these empty things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything that is in them.
en.R: We are only human beings, just like you! We are telling you good news. We want you to stop worshiping these useless gods and turn to the living God. He made the sky, the earth, the sea and everything in them.

fr.L: Nous aussi, nous sommes des {{gender:humains|hommes}} de même nature que vous, et nous vous annonçons l’Évangile : que vous vous détourniez de ces choses vaines vers [le] Dieu vivant, qui a fait le ciel et la terre et la mer et tout ce qui s’y trouve ;
fr.B: Nous sommes des mortels, de même nature que vous. Nous sommes venus avec l’Évangile, pour vous appeler à quitter ces choses vaines et à vous tourner vers le Dieu vivant, qui a fait le ciel et la terre, la mer et tout ce qui s’y trouve.
fr.R: Nous ne sommes que des êtres humains, exactement comme vous ! Nous vous annonçons une bonne nouvelle. Nous voulons que vous arrêtiez d’adorer ces faux dieux inutiles et que vous vous tourniez vers le Dieu vivant. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a fait le ciel, la terre, la mer et tout ce qu’ils contiennent.

es.L: También nosotros somos {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}} de la misma naturaleza que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos la buena noticia de que {{plural_you:se vuelvan|os volváis}} de estas cosas vanas al Dios vivo, que hizo el cielo y la tierra y el mar y todo lo que hay en ellos;
es.B: Nosotros también somos mortales, de la misma naturaleza que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} anunciamos la buena noticia para que {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} estas cosas vanas y {{plural_you:se vuelvan|os volváis}} al Dios vivo, que hizo el cielo, la tierra, el mar y todo lo que hay en ellos.
es.R: ¡Nosotros somos solo seres humanos, igual que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} estamos anunciando una buena noticia. Queremos que {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de adorar a estos dioses que no sirven para nada y que {{plural_you:se vuelvan|os volváis}} al Dios vivo. Él hizo el cielo, la tierra, el mar y todo lo que hay en ellos.

sw.L: Sisi nasi ni wanadamu wenye hali moja na ninyi, tukiwahubiri habari njema kwamba mgeuke kutoka katika mambo haya yasiyo na maana, mmwelekee Mungu aliye hai, aliyeumba mbingu na nchi na bahari na vyote vilivyo ndani yake;
sw.B: Sisi pia ni wanadamu tu, wenye hali ileile kama ninyi. Tumekuja na habari njema, tukiwaita mwache mambo haya yasiyo na faida, mmgeukie Mungu aliye hai, aliyeumba mbingu na dunia na bahari, na kila kitu kilichomo ndani yake.
sw.R: Sisi ni wanadamu tu, kama ninyi! Tunawaletea habari njema. Tunataka muache kuabudu miungu hii isiyo na faida, mmgeukie Mungu aliye hai. Yeye ndiye aliyeumba anga, dunia, bahari na kila kitu kilichomo.

decisions.choice: of like nature: having the same nature, subject to the same weakness
decisions.reason: The word is used of Elijah, a man with a nature like ours (James 5:17). The apostles are not gods but mortals.

decisions.choice: empty things: idols and the worship given them
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament calls idols empty things (1 Kings 16:13, 16:26). The point is the sacrifice the crowd was preparing.

decisions.choice: turn to the living God: leave the idols for the God who lives
decisions.reason: The living God is set against lifeless idols. Paul describes the same turning in 1 Thessalonians 1:9.

decisions.choice: who made heaven and earth and sea and all in them: words from Exodus 20:11 and Psalm 146:6
decisions.reason: The apostles speak to people who did not know the Scriptures, but the words are those of Israel's confession of God the Creator. Acts 4:24 uses them in prayer.

decisions.choice: humans, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings as against gods. Balanced says "mortals" and Readable "human beings", which already include everyone.

decisions.choice: stop worshiping these useless gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what the empty things are, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a fait
alternatives: Il a fait, with no span
decisions.reason: The English Readable begins a new sentence with a plain "He". French "C’est lui qui" gives the emphasis the relative clause carries, and "lui" then stands inside the sentence, so it takes the span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}
decisions.reason: As in 14:11: the inclusive form is the default and "hombres" the alternative.

source.text: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: who in the having passed generations allowed all the nations to go in the ways of them;

en.L: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to go their own ways;
en.B: In past generations {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} allowed every nation to walk in its own ways.
en.R: In the past, God let all the nations live the way they wanted to.

fr.L: qui, dans les générations passées, a laissé toutes les nations suivre leurs propres chemins ;
fr.B: Dans les générations passées, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a laissé chaque nation suivre ses propres chemins.
fr.R: Autrefois, Dieu a laissé toutes les nations vivre comme elles le voulaient.

es.L: el cual, en las generaciones pasadas, permitió que todas las naciones anduvieran por sus propios caminos;
es.B: En las generaciones pasadas, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} permitió que todas las naciones siguieran sus propios caminos.
es.R: En el pasado, Dios dejó que todas las naciones vivieran como quisieran.

sw.L: ambaye katika vizazi vilivyopita aliyaacha mataifa yote yaende katika njia zao wenyewe;
sw.B: Katika vizazi vilivyopita aliyaacha mataifa yote yafuate njia zao wenyewe.
sw.R: Zamani Mungu aliyaacha mataifa yote yaishi kama yalivyotaka.

decisions.choice: allowed: God let them go their way without stepping in to judge them
decisions.reason: Paul says the same at Athens: God overlooked the times of ignorance, but now calls everyone to turn (17:30). The past patience is not approval.

decisions.choice: all the nations: all the peoples outside Israel
decisions.reason: The nations, the Gentile peoples, who did not have the law and the prophets.

decisions.choice: to go in their ways: to live as they chose
decisions.reason: Walking in a way is a common biblical picture for a way of life.

decisions.choice: a new sentence beginning "In past generations he"
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long sentence of 14:15-17 into shorter ones.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God instead of using a relative pronoun.

source.text: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: and yet not without witness himself he left, doing good, from heaven to you rains giving and seasons fruitful, filling with food and gladness the hearts of you.

en.L: and yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not leave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} without witness, doing good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness."
en.B: Even so, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has not left {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} without a witness. He does you good: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives you rain from the sky and seasons that bear fruit, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fills you with food and your hearts with gladness."
en.R: But God has always shown you what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is like. He does good things for you. He sends you rain from the sky. He makes your crops grow at the right times. He gives you plenty of food and makes you happy."

fr.L: et pourtant {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est pas laissé sans témoignage, faisant du bien, vous donnant du ciel des pluies et des saisons fertiles, remplissant vos cœurs de nourriture et de joie. »
fr.B: Pourtant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est pas laissé sans témoin : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous fait du bien, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donne du ciel la pluie et des saisons qui portent du fruit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous comble de nourriture et remplit vos cœurs de joie. »
fr.R: Mais Dieu vous a toujours montré qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est. Il vous fait du bien. Il vous envoie la pluie du ciel. Il fait pousser vos récoltes au bon moment. Il vous donne de la nourriture en abondance et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous rend heureux. »

es.L: y sin embargo no se dejó a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} sin testimonio, haciendo el bien, {{plural_you:dándoles|dándoos}} lluvias del cielo y estaciones fructíferas, llenando de alimento y de alegría {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones».
es.B: Aun así, no ha dejado de dar testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}}: {{plural_you:les|os}} hace bien, {{plural_you:les|os}} da lluvias del cielo y estaciones que dan fruto, y {{plural_you:los|os}} colma de alimento y llena de alegría {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones».
es.R: Pero Dios siempre {{plural_you:les|os}} ha mostrado cómo es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Hace cosas buenas por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} manda lluvia del cielo. Hace que {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} cosechas crezcan en el tiempo oportuno. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} da comida en abundancia y {{plural_you:los|os}} hace felices».

sw.L: lakini hakujiacha bila ushahidi, akitenda mema, akiwapa mvua kutoka mbinguni na majira ya kuzaa matunda, akiijaza mioyo yenu chakula na furaha."
sw.B: Hata hivyo, hakujiacha bila ushahidi. Anawatendea mema: anawapa mvua kutoka angani na majira ya mavuno, anawashibisha kwa chakula na kuijaza mioyo yenu furaha."
sw.R: Lakini siku zote Mungu amewaonyesha {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni wa namna gani. Anawatendea mambo mema. Anawanyeshea mvua kutoka angani. Anayafanya mazao yenu yakue wakati unaofaa. Anawapa chakula kingi na kuwafanya mfurahi."

decisions.choice: not without witness: God has given evidence of himself
decisions.reason: The witness is not a person but the good things God does. Romans 1:20 says God's power can be seen in what he made.

decisions.choice: doing good, giving, filling: the ways God has borne witness
decisions.reason: The three participles explain how God left a witness to himself: in rain, harvests and food.

decisions.choice: filling your hearts with food and gladness: satisfying you with food and making you glad
decisions.reason: One verb covers both things. The heart stands for the whole person, so the phrase means God satisfies people's needs and gives them joy in life.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "you" and "your hearts"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "us" and "our". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: fills you with food and your hearts with gladness
alternatives: filling your hearts with food and gladness
decisions.reason: Balanced gives each noun its natural English object, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: God has always shown you what he is like
alternatives: he did not leave himself without witness
decisions.reason: Readable says what the witness is: God showed himself through his goodness.

decisions.choice: the reflexive {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}} carries the span
decisions.reason: French says "he did not leave himself" with the reflexive verb "se laisser", so the span the English puts on "himself" goes on "s’". "Lui-même" would need a heavier rewording.

decisions.choice: hakujiacha, with no span
decisions.reason: Swahili says "himself" with the reflexive -ji- inside the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the English "himself" span has no Swahili counterpart; the free pronoun "yeye" at Readable takes the span.

source.text: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And these things saying hardly they stopped the crowds of not to sacrifice to them.

en.L: And saying these things, they barely restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.
en.B: Saying these things, they could hardly hold the crowds back from offering sacrifice to them.
en.R: Paul and Barnabas said all this, but it was still hard for them to stop the people from offering animals to them as if they were gods.

fr.L: Et, disant ces choses, ils empêchèrent à grand-peine les foules de leur offrir un sacrifice.
fr.B: Même en parlant ainsi, ils eurent bien du mal à empêcher les foules de leur offrir un sacrifice.
fr.R: Paul et Barnabas ont dit tout cela, mais ils ont encore eu du mal à empêcher les gens de leur offrir des animaux comme s’ils étaient des dieux.

es.L: Y diciendo estas cosas, a duras penas impidieron que las multitudes les ofrecieran sacrificios.
es.B: Aun diciendo esto, apenas pudieron impedir que la multitud les ofreciera sacrificios.
es.R: Pablo y Bernabé dijeron todo esto, pero aun así les costó mucho impedir que la gente les ofreciera animales como si fueran dioses.

sw.L: Na wakisema mambo haya, kwa shida waliyazuia makutano wasiwatolee dhabihu.
sw.B: Hata kwa maneno hayo, waliweza kwa shida tu kuyazuia makutano wasiwatolee dhabihu.
sw.R: Paulo na Barnaba walisema hayo yote, lakini bado ilikuwa vigumu kuwazuia watu wasiwatolee wanyama kama sadaka, kana kwamba wao ni miungu.

decisions.choice: hardly: only with great difficulty
decisions.reason: They succeeded, but only just.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the verse ends with "to them"
alternatives: some manuscripts add "but that each should go home"
decisions.reason: Some witnesses, among them Codex Bezae, add that the crowds were sent home. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: offering animals to them as if they were gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sacrifice meant, as 14:11-13 shows.

source.text: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.

records.literal_gloss: Came upon but from Antioch and Iconium Jews, and having persuaded the crowds and having stoned the Paul, they were dragging [him] outside the city, supposing him to have died.

en.L: But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having won over the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged [him] outside the city, supposing that he had died.
en.B: But Jews from Antioch and Iconium came on the scene and persuaded the crowds. They stoned Paul and hauled him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
en.R: But some Jews came there from Antioch and Iconium. They talked the crowds into turning against Paul. The people threw stones at Paul. Then they dragged him outside the city, because they thought he was dead.

fr.L: Mais des Juifs arrivèrent d’Antioche et d’Iconium, et ayant gagné les foules et lapidé Paul, ils [le] traînaient hors de la ville, pensant qu’il était mort.
fr.B: Mais des Juifs d’Antioche et d’Iconium survinrent et persuadèrent les foules. Ils lapidèrent Paul et le traînèrent hors de la ville, pensant qu’il était mort.
fr.R: Mais des Juifs sont venus d’Antioche et d’Iconium. Ils ont poussé les foules à se retourner contre Paul. Les gens ont jeté des pierres sur Paul. Puis ils l’ont traîné hors de la ville, parce qu’ils croyaient qu’il était mort.

es.L: Pero llegaron unos judíos de Antioquía y de Iconio, y habiendo persuadido a las multitudes y apedreado a Pablo, [lo] arrastraban fuera de la ciudad, pensando que había muerto.
es.B: Pero llegaron unos judíos de Antioquía y de Iconio y convencieron a la multitud. Apedrearon a Pablo y lo sacaron a rastras de la ciudad, creyendo que estaba muerto.
es.R: Pero algunos judíos llegaron allí desde Antioquía e Iconio. Convencieron a la gente para que se pusiera en contra de Pablo. La gente le tiró piedras a Pablo. Luego lo arrastraron fuera de la ciudad, porque creían que estaba muerto.

sw.L: Lakini Wayahudi walifika kutoka Antiokia na Ikonio, na wakiisha kuyashawishi makutano na kumpiga Paulo kwa mawe, walimburuta nje ya mji, wakidhani kwamba amekufa.
sw.B: Lakini Wayahudi kutoka Antiokia na Ikonio walifika, wakayashawishi makutano. Wakampiga Paulo kwa mawe, wakamkokota nje ya mji, wakidhani kwamba amekufa.
sw.R: Lakini baadhi ya Wayahudi walifika huko kutoka Antiokia na Ikonio. Wakawashawishi watu wamgeuke Paulo. Watu wakampiga Paulo kwa mawe. Kisha wakamburuta nje ya mji, kwa sababu walidhani amekufa.

decisions.choice: Antioch and Iconium: Pisidian Antioch (13:14) and Iconium (14:1)
decisions.reason: These are the cities Paul and Barnabas had just been driven from (13:50; 14:5-6). Their opponents followed them a long way.

decisions.choice: they stoned Paul: the stoning Paul later recalls
decisions.reason: Paul writes, "once I was stoned" (2 Corinthians 11:25), and recalls what happened to him at Antioch, Iconium and Lystra (2 Timothy 3:11).

decisions.choice: supposing he had died: they thought he was dead
decisions.reason: Luke reports what the crowd thought. He does not say that Paul died.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the shorter text
alternatives: Codex Bezae and related witnesses expand the verse
decisions.reason: The Western text says the Jews came while the apostles were staying and teaching, and persuaded the crowds by saying the apostles spoke nothing true. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: talked the crowds into turning against Paul
decisions.reason: Readable says what the crowds were persuaded to do.

source.text: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having surrounded but the disciples him, having risen up he entered into the city.

en.L: But when the disciples had surrounded him, he got up and went into the city.
en.B: But when the disciples stood in a circle around him, he rose and went back into the city.
en.R: But the believers gathered around Paul. Then he got up and went back into the town.

fr.L: Mais les disciples l’ayant entouré, il se leva et entra dans la ville.
fr.B: Mais quand les disciples se furent rassemblés autour de lui, il se releva et rentra dans la ville.
fr.R: Mais les croyants se sont réunis autour de Paul. Alors il s’est relevé et il est retourné dans la ville.

es.L: Pero rodeándolo los discípulos, se levantó y entró en la ciudad.
es.B: Pero cuando los discípulos se pusieron alrededor de él, se levantó y volvió a entrar en la ciudad.
es.R: Pero los discípulos se reunieron alrededor de Pablo. Entonces él se levantó y volvió a entrar en la ciudad.

sw.L: Lakini wanafunzi walipomzunguka, aliinuka, akaingia mjini.
sw.B: Lakini wanafunzi walipokuwa wamesimama wakimzunguka, aliinuka, akarudi mjini.
sw.R: Lakini wanafunzi walikusanyika kumzunguka Paulo. Kisha akainuka, akarudi mjini.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the new believers at Lystra
decisions.reason: Luke has not mentioned believers at Lystra, but the preaching of 14:7 had made some. Timothy was from Lystra (16:1-2), and 2 Timothy 3:10-11 says he knew of Paul's sufferings there; whether he was in this group the text does not say.

decisions.choice: he got up: he stood up and walked back into the city
alternatives: he was raised from the dead
decisions.reason: Luke tells the recovery plainly and without calling it a miracle, but that a stoned man could get up and walk was remarkable.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for followers of Jesus.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: "discípulos" at every level, Readable included, where the English Readable says "the believers".

decisions.choice: wanafunzi (R)
decisions.reason: "Wanafunzi" is kept at every level, as the project's Swahili term list settles, where the English Readable says "believers"; the same in 14:21-22 and 14:28.

source.text: καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρναβᾷ εἰς Δέρβην.

records.literal_gloss: And on the next day he went out with the Barnabas to Derbe.

en.L: And on the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
en.B: The next day he set out with Barnabas for Derbe.
en.R: The next day Paul and Barnabas left for Derbe.

fr.L: Et le lendemain, il partit avec Barnabas pour Derbe.
fr.B: Le jour suivant, il se mit en route avec Barnabas vers Derbe.
fr.R: Le lendemain, Paul et Barnabas sont partis pour Derbe.

es.L: Y al día siguiente salió con Bernabé hacia Derbe.
es.B: Al día siguiente partió con Bernabé rumbo a Derbe.
es.R: Al día siguiente, Pablo y Bernabé se fueron a Derbe.

sw.L: Na siku iliyofuata alitoka pamoja na Barnaba kwenda Derbe.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata aliondoka pamoja na Barnaba kwenda Derbe.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata Paulo na Barnaba waliondoka kwenda Derbe.

decisions.choice: Derbe: a town of Lycaonia, east of Lystra
decisions.reason: Derbe was the farthest point of this journey (14:6). From there they turned back (14:21).

decisions.choice: on the next day: he was able to travel at once
decisions.reason: The short time stresses how fully he recovered.

source.text: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having preached the gospel and the city that and having made disciples many, they returned to the Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch, \v 22 strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting to remain in the faith, and that through many afflictions it is necessary [for] us to enter into the kingdom of the God.

en.L: And having preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch, \v 22 strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting [them] to remain in the faith, and [saying] that through many afflictions we must enter into the kingdom of God.
en.B: They proclaimed the gospel in that city and made many disciples. After that they retraced their steps to Lystra, to Iconium and to Antioch. \v 22 They made the disciples strong in spirit and urged them to hold on to the faith, saying, "We must enter the kingdom of God by way of many afflictions."
en.R: Paul and Barnabas told the good news in Derbe, and many people there became followers of Jesus. Then Paul and Barnabas went back to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch. \v 22 In each place they helped the believers grow strong inside. They urged them to keep their faith. They said, "We will have to go through many troubles before we enter God's kingdom."

fr.L: Et ayant annoncé l’Évangile à cette ville et fait bon nombre de disciples, ils retournèrent à Lystre, à Iconium et à Antioche, \v 22 affermissant les âmes des disciples, [les] exhortant à demeurer dans la foi, et [disant] que par beaucoup de tribulations il nous faut entrer dans le royaume de Dieu.
fr.B: Ils annoncèrent l’Évangile dans cette ville et y firent de nombreux disciples. Puis ils revinrent sur leurs pas, à Lystre, à Iconium et à Antioche. \v 22 Ils affermirent le courage des disciples et les exhortèrent à rester fermes dans la foi, en disant : « C’est en passant par bien des épreuves qu’il nous faut entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.R: Paul et Barnabas ont annoncé la bonne nouvelle à Derbe, et beaucoup de gens se sont mis à suivre Jésus. Ensuite, Paul et Barnabas sont retournés à Lystre, à Iconium et à Antioche. \v 22 Dans chaque ville, ils ont aidé les croyants à devenir forts intérieurement. Ils les ont encouragés à garder leur foi. Ils disaient : « Nous devrons traverser beaucoup de difficultés avant d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »

es.L: Y habiendo anunciado la buena noticia a aquella ciudad y hecho muchos discípulos, regresaron a Listra, a Iconio y a Antioquía, \v 22 fortaleciendo las almas de los discípulos, exhortándolos a permanecer en la fe, y [diciendo] que es necesario que a través de muchas tribulaciones entremos en el reino de Dios.
es.B: Anunciaron la buena noticia en aquella ciudad e hicieron muchos discípulos. Después volvieron sobre sus pasos a Listra, a Iconio y a Antioquía. \v 22 Fortalecían el ánimo de los discípulos y los exhortaban a mantenerse firmes en la fe, diciendo: «Es necesario que pasemos por muchas tribulaciones para entrar en el reino de Dios».
es.R: Pablo y Bernabé anunciaron la buena noticia en Derbe, y muchas personas de allí se hicieron discípulos de Jesús. Luego Pablo y Bernabé volvieron a Listra, Iconio y Antioquía. \v 22 En cada lugar ayudaban a los discípulos a hacerse fuertes por dentro. Los animaban a seguir firmes en la fe. Les decían: «Tendremos que pasar por muchos sufrimientos antes de entrar en el reino de Dios».

sw.L: Na wakiisha kuhubiri habari njema katika mji ule na kufanya wanafunzi wengi, walirudi Listra na Ikonio na Antiokia, \v 22 wakiziimarisha nafsi za wanafunzi, wakiwahimiza kudumu katika imani, na [wakisema] kwamba kupitia dhiki nyingi imetupasa kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu.
sw.B: Walihubiri habari njema katika mji huo, wakafanya wanafunzi wengi. Kisha wakarudi Listra, Ikonio na Antiokia. \v 22 Waliwaimarisha wanafunzi katika nafsi zao na kuwahimiza wadumu katika imani, wakisema, "Imetupasa kupitia dhiki nyingi ndipo tuingie katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Paulo na Barnaba waliwaambia watu wa Derbe habari njema, na watu wengi huko wakawa wanafunzi wa Yesu. Kisha Paulo na Barnaba walirudi Listra, Ikonio na Antiokia. \v 22 Kila mahali waliwasaidia wanafunzi wawe imara ndani ya mioyo yao. Waliwahimiza waendelee kuamini. Wakasema, "Ni lazima tupitie taabu nyingi kabla ya kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."

decisions.choice: made many disciples: brought many people to follow Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone a disciple (Matthew 28:19).

decisions.choice: they returned: back through the cities they had been driven from
alternatives: they went home by another road
decisions.reason: Derbe was near the road through the Cilician Gates to Tarsus and Syria. Instead they went back through Lystra, Iconium and Antioch to care for the new believers.

decisions.choice: strengthening the souls: making the disciples strong in their inner life
decisions.reason: The soul here is the inner self. The same verb is used in 15:32 and 15:41 of strengthening the churches.

decisions.choice: to remain in the faith: to keep on believing
alternatives: to keep the body of Christian teaching
decisions.reason: "The faith" can mean trust in Jesus or what Christians believe. Here, with "remain in", the believers' own trust is meant, as in 11:23 and 13:43.

decisions.choice: we must enter the kingdom of God through many afflictions: suffering is part of the way, by God's plan
alternatives: suffering earns entry to the kingdom
decisions.reason: "Must" in Luke-Acts often marks what God has planned (Luke 24:26). The kingdom of God is God's rule, which believers will enter in full when it comes. The word "afflictions" means pressures and troubles, such as Paul had just suffered.

decisions.choice: we: the apostles and the believers together
decisions.reason: The words switch to direct speech: this is what the apostles said. It is not one of the "we" passages of Acts.

decisions.choice: direct speech in quotation marks
decisions.reason: The Greek shifts to "us", so the apostles' own words are being reported. Literal keeps the indirect form.

decisions.choice: in Derbe; many people there became followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the town and says what making disciples means.

decisions.choice: tribulations (L); épreuves (B); difficultés (R)
decisions.reason: "Tribulations" keeps the traditional weight of the Greek at Literal; "épreuves" is the usual word for hardships a believer goes through; Readable uses the everyday word. "Persécutions" would narrow the sense to attacks from others.

decisions.choice: se hicieron discípulos de Jesús; los discípulos
decisions.reason: "Discípulos" at every level, as in 14:20, where the English Readable says "followers" and "believers".

decisions.choice: nafsi
decisions.reason: The inner life of the disciples (meaning decision); "nafsi" is used rather than "roho", which the Swahili drafts keep for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit.

decisions.choice: dhiki (L, B); taabu (R)
decisions.reason: "Dhiki" for afflictions, as in 7:10-11 and 11:19; Readable uses the everyday "taabu" (troubles), as the English Readable does.

source.text: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.

records.literal_gloss: Having appointed by hand-stretching now for them in each church elders, having prayed with fastings, they committed them to the Lord in whom they had believed.

en.L: And when they had appointed elders for them in every church, having prayed with fasting, they committed them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
en.B: In each church they appointed elders for the believers, and after praying and fasting, they placed them in the care of the Lord in whom they had believed.
en.R: In each church Paul and Barnabas chose leaders called elders. They prayed and fasted. Then they put the believers in the care of the Lord, the one they had believed in.

fr.L: Et leur ayant désigné des anciens dans chaque église, ayant prié avec des jeûnes, ils les confièrent au Seigneur en qui ils avaient cru.
fr.B: Dans chaque église, ils désignèrent des anciens pour les croyants, et après avoir prié et jeûné, ils les confièrent aux soins du Seigneur en qui ils avaient cru.
fr.R: Dans chaque église, Paul et Barnabas ont choisi des responsables qu’on appelait des anciens. Ils ont prié et jeûné. Puis ils ont confié les croyants au Seigneur, celui en qui ils avaient cru.

es.L: Y habiéndoles designado ancianos en cada iglesia, habiendo orado con ayunos, los encomendaron al Señor en quien habían creído.
es.B: En cada iglesia les nombraron ancianos y, después de orar y ayunar, los encomendaron al Señor en quien habían creído.
es.R: En cada iglesia, Pablo y Bernabé escogieron a líderes llamados ancianos. Oraron y ayunaron. Luego pusieron a los creyentes en las manos del Señor, en quien habían creído.

sw.L: Na wakiisha kuwachagulia wazee katika kila kanisa, wakiisha kuomba pamoja na kufunga, waliwakabidhi kwa Bwana ambaye walikuwa wamemwamini.
sw.B: Katika kila kanisa waliwachagulia waumini wazee, na baada ya kuomba na kufunga, wakawaweka chini ya ulinzi wa Bwana waliyekuwa wamemwamini.
sw.R: Katika kila kanisa Paulo na Barnaba walichagua viongozi walioitwa wazee. Waliomba na kufunga. Kisha wakawaweka waumini mikononi mwa Bwana, yule waliyekuwa wamemwamini.

decisions.choice: appointed: chose and put into office
alternatives: elected by a show of hands of the church
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to vote by stretching out the hand, and came to mean to choose or appoint. In 2 Corinthians 8:19 a man is chosen by the churches. Here Paul and Barnabas are the subject, so they appointed the elders; whether the church had a voice in the choice the text does not say.

decisions.choice: elders: leaders of the local church
decisions.reason: Jewish synagogues and towns were led by elders, and the church in Jerusalem had elders (11:30). Paul later calls the elders of Ephesus overseers who shepherd the church (20:17, 20:28).

decisions.choice: prayer with fasting: as when Paul and Barnabas were sent out
decisions.reason: The church at Antioch fasted and prayed before sending them (13:2-3). The apostles now do the same for the new leaders.

decisions.choice: them: all the believers, elders included
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally takes in the believers of each church, who had believed in the Lord. The elders were among them.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, in whom they had believed
decisions.reason: In Acts people believe in the Lord Jesus (11:17, 16:31).

decisions.choice: leaders called elders
decisions.reason: Readable says what elders were.

decisions.choice: l’église (lowercase) for each local church; les anciens
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles: a single congregation is "l’église" in lowercase, the whole body of believers "l’Église". "Les anciens" is the plain French for the elders; "presbytres" is a technical term.

decisions.choice: wazee (L, B); viongozi walioitwa wazee (R)
decisions.reason: The church office, as the term list has it ("wazee"); Readable follows the English Readable's "leaders called elders" so the title is still heard.

source.text: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν, καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν, κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having passed through the Pisidia they came to the Pamphylia, \v 25 and having spoken in Perga the word they went down to Attalia, \v 26 and from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been handed over to the grace of the God for the work which they fulfilled.

en.L: And passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia, \v 25 and having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia, \v 26 and from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work that they had fulfilled.
en.B: They crossed Pisidia and came into Pamphylia, \v 25 and when they had spoken the word in Perga they went down to Attalia. \v 26 From there they set sail for Antioch, the place where they had first been entrusted to God's grace for the task that they had now carried out to the end.
en.R: They traveled through the area called Pisidia and came to Pamphylia. \v 25 They told people God's message in the town of Perga. Then they went down to the coast at Attalia. \v 26 From there they sailed back to Antioch in Syria. That was where the believers had prayed and given them over to God's grace for this work. Now they had finished the work.

fr.L: Et ayant traversé la Pisidie, ils vinrent en Pamphylie, \v 25 et ayant annoncé la parole à Pergé, ils descendirent à Attalie, \v 26 et de là ils firent voile vers Antioche, d’où ils avaient été remis à la grâce de Dieu pour l’œuvre qu’ils avaient accomplie.
fr.B: Ils traversèrent la Pisidie et arrivèrent en Pamphylie. \v 25 Après avoir annoncé la parole à Pergé, ils descendirent à Attalie. \v 26 De là, ils s’embarquèrent pour Antioche, d’où ils avaient d’abord été confiés à la grâce de Dieu pour la tâche qu’ils venaient de mener à bien.
fr.R: Ils ont traversé la région appelée Pisidie et sont arrivés en Pamphylie. \v 25 Ils ont annoncé le message de Dieu dans la ville de Pergé.
